records.question: HCP Data Graph Methodology/Foundation
records.answer:
PulsePoint’s HCP database is backed by direct opt-in consent via Medscape. Because we are the same company, HCPs registering and opting in with Medscape are also opting in directly with PulsePoint. This is unique and differentiated from any other HCP solution in the market, who rely on buying HCP data with no direct opt-in consent and no way to validate the data they are receiving. In other words, it’s the only guaranteed deterministic network of HCPs available to a programmatic platform. It also means we have direct unique access to HCPs not available for targeting elsewhere.
 
PulsePoint takes our direct opt-in, registered HCPs and takes their email addresses to create a profile for each NPI.  This personal information is encrypted in our clean room and we work with companies like LiveRamp and ID5 to connect all types of device identifiers to each NPI.  We also track opt-outs.  Anytime a user opts out, at any point of their journey, all of the users' other devices are opted out as well.
 
On top of this exclusive first party dataset, sits our knowledge graph, where we pull in direct relevant data about the experiences your target oncology HCPs are having on Medscape. What conditions they’re researching, which drug monographs they’re visiting, which fast 5 quizzes are they taking, even patients identifying physicians on WebMD Find a Doc. All of this data is used to train our Ai models to optimize towards receptivity. Not just reaching HCPs because they’re on the list, but reaching them at exactly the moment where we can maximize the impact.

records.question: With the competitive digital landscape across platforms, what are keys areas of focus in terms of your platform's differentiators in the marketplace?
records.answer:
PulsePoint is the programmatic arm of Internet brands, owner of WebMD/Medscape, and the leader in the health marketing space leveraging proprietary software, data, and analytics to effectively reach your target audience via display, video, native, CTV, and more.
 
 PulsePoint entire product suite sits on top of a unique, differentiated data foundation consisting of a proprietary first party identity graph, clinical data and the Medscape/WebMD integration. The combination of these three data pillars is different from any other programmatic partner and enables our clients to leverage a deep repository of 1st party data to plan, activate, optimize, and measure media campaigns all through one platform. This massive differentiator is one of the leading reasons that PulsePoint has over 80% of the HCP programmatic spend across the pharma landscape and is leading to a similar trend with consumer activation.
 
 Because of a unique partnership with Medscape, PulsePoint is the only DSP capable of activating Programmatic guaranteed buys accessing Medscape inventory. We have an identity graph informed by first-party data through our parent companies WebMD and Medscape, making our offerings future-proofed for the cookie apocalypse. Our contextualizer is mapped to the National Institute of Health’s MESH taxonomy, allowing us to build out 3,500+ condition-based audience segments. We can target, measure, and report based on 1:1 NPI level against 3.2M NPIs. With our access to claims data, we can target physicians based on certain Dx, Tx, and Rx behaviors. Additionally, we can reach diagnosed patients who are also actively reading about their condition - combining our proprietary contextual technology with raw claims data. 
 
 PulsePoint's programmatic platform integrates seamlessly with our HCP analytics technology, HCP365, which is backed by a database of over 3 million NPIs with active, named opt-in consent. Utilizing proprietary methodologies, HCP365 maps NPIs across various screens and devices, unifying cross-channel insights and providing analysis at the individual HCP level for precise 1:1 attribution. Identified HCPs can then be automatically remarketed to based on predefined business rules.
 
 HCP: PulsePoint is the only fully consented and deterministic activation platform with the ability to identify and provide NPI and clinical behavior targeting for authenticated NPI's.
 DTC: PulsePoint is the only first-party validated platform providing a journey-based product suite of targeting and attribution technology. PulsePoint operates both a contextual as well as a deterministic DTC Platform. Similarly, accessing Medscape through the LIFE platform WebMD inventory is also available on LIFE. In addition, WebMD-based audiences (patients visiting WebMD) will be available to Heartbeat.
 Crosswalk: PulsePoint's technology, leveraging signals from WebMD, Medscape, and other digitally and clinically relevant sources, is positioned to take advantage of the natural synergy between HCP and DTC audiences who are intrinsically connected throughout the journey toward better overall health outcomes. We enable your agency with the ability to leverage HCP data and insights to inform DTC targeting and vice versa. This includes solutions customized for clients to reach both the HCPs on the target list and their patients at optimal points in the journey, including at the point of care, between appointments, and in locations where HCPs are seeing a high influx of patients with specific symptoms.

records.question: The state data privacy landscape is continually evolving. How do you stay on top of these developments and collaborate with your clients to ensure compliance with those laws as you assess media opportunities and use of personal data?
records.answer:
• We are actively monitoring all new privacy laws and their effective dates, and our legal team reviews the laws and analyzes what needs to be changed in our products, processes and public-facing disclosures.
• We have, and will continue to, update our privacy policy in order to adhere to requirements of the applicable state laws.
• We have implemented the applicable tech specs to recognize GPP (from the IAB), GDPR, CCPA, and other consent strings.
• PulsePoint is a signatory to the MSPA (from the IAB), which helps aid in ensuring contractual obligations are in place as required by the new state privacy laws.
• PulsePoint has implemented and uses OneTrust as its Consent Management Platform, which includes cookie management and opt-outs for its owned and operated sites.
• We have increased our geotargeting radius to 2006 ft (.38 miles) for all states in the US, as most new privacy laws include a definition of “Precise Geolocation” - the exact distance varies from state to state, so we have implemented a 2006 ft radius distance to ensure compliance with all states.
• We have removed certain product availability to comply with states’ new prohibitions on geofencing around in-person health care facilities.
• Our product and tech teams regularly review products with legal counsel to ensure compliance with US privacy laws, including HIPAA, FTC, etc.
• Our legal team has created processes in conjunction with the business teams to ensure we review any cases where sensitive information or PHI may potentially be collected, and then take the appropriate steps to ensure security and privacy of that information.
• We honor all validated opt outs received by consumers, both via CMPs and AdChoices as well as emails to our privacy@pulsepoint.com inbox.

records.question: What targeting settings can advertisers place to inform the forecasting tool? Please list.
records.answer:
Advertisers can apply various targeting settings in the PulsePoint Media Planner tool to inform forecasting and gain more accurate predictions of campaign outcomes. These settings allow advertisers to tailor their forecasts based on specific audiences, geography, and inventory preferences. Here are the key targeting settings available:
 
 Audience Segments:
 - First-Party Data: Custom audiences created from your first-party data, such as CRM lists or website visitors, can be uploaded and used for targeting and forecasting.
 - Proprietary PulsePoint Audiences: Access to pre-built health-related audience segments, including those based on de-identified consumer behavior, health conditions, or HCP (Healthcare Professional) profiles.
 - Third-Party Data: Advertisers can apply third-party segments from data providers like Crossix, LiveRamp, or Swoop to inform audience reach.
 
 Geographic Targeting:
 - Zip Code Level Targeting: Advertisers can target specific geographic areas down to the zip code level.
 - Radius Targeting: Set geographic radius targeting to reach individuals within a certain proximity to a location.
 - Country, State, and DMA (Designated Market Area): Broader geographic targeting settings for national or regional campaigns.
 
 Demographic and Behavioral Targeting:
 - Age, Gender, and Ethnicity: Apply demographic filters based on the specific target consumer.
 - Behavioral Segmentation: Set targeting based on specific behaviors, including online engagement with health-related content or browsing activity related to certain conditions.
 
 Device and Inventory Type:
 - Device Type: Target users on specific devices, such as desktop, mobile, tablet, or connected TV (CTV).
 - Channel/Inventory Type: Forecast impressions across different channels, including display, video, CTV, DOOH (Digital Out-of-Home), audio, or endemic sites.
 
 Contextual Targeting:
 - Keywords and Page Context: Use PulsePoint’s proprietary contextualizer tool to target based on the context of the pages or keywords users are engaging with, particularly around health-related content.
 - Condition-Based Segments: Target based on specific health conditions using classifications from NIH's MeSH taxonomy.
 
 Frequency Capping and Recency:
 - Frequency Caps: Control how often your ads will be shown to the same user within a given time period to manage exposure and avoid over-delivery.
 - Recency Windows: Set time windows to target users who have engaged with relevant content within the past 3, 7, or 30 days.
 
 Bid and Budget Parameters:
 - Bid CPM: Set the expected cost per thousand impressions (CPM) to inform cost forecasting.
 - Flight Dates: Define the campaign’s start and end dates to align forecasting with your campaign timeline.
 
 These targeting settings can all be adjusted within the Media Planner tool to provide advertisers with a tailored forecast that aligns with their specific audience and campaign goals.

records.question: Are you able to target by medical condition or ailment and remain HIPAA compliant?
records.answer: • Yes - PulsePoint Clinical targeting is HIPAA Compliant because it is based on modeled claims data, using individualized digital activity is de-identified through a propensity map where sensitive information is dropped from claims files and where geo, zip codes, etc. become individual identifiers. Individual digital activity is de-identified through tokenization where an individual’s PII is stripped and replaced by a unique token. Through our propensity map, we can pinpoint individuals living in a zip code with a target condition in a privacy-safe way. The tokenization and propensity map processes de-identify individuals and are not reversible to re-identify audiences later on which makes it HIPAA Compliant.

records.question: Describe your process to create audiences/segments/models intended to be used to market healthcare services. Please include the names of any providers of consumer data that you use to build your product/service.
records.answer:
For HCP, we operate in a 1-1 NPI based targeting manor with no modeling needed
 
 For DTC, we offer either contextual based or clinical-model based targeting solutions. The custom claims-based models are based on a database of 220MM+ consumers and 3BB annual pharmacy claims. In a clean room where private information is anonymized, millions of demographic and location identifiers are used to segment groups of individuals with similar attributes. To help determine brand-relevance, consumers’ digital activity is also considered, derived from contextualizing the pages, apps, and environments sending us 200B requests daily, including PulsePoint’s proprietary access to first-party endemic content engagement on Internet Brand owned and operated sites like WebMD.

records.question: What are your contextual capabilities?
records.answer:
Our patented health contextual technology is mapped to the National Institute of Health’s MESH taxonomy, allowing us to build out 3,500+ condition-based audience segments.
 
 • Health Pages: Capture the consumer & patient’s attention the exact moment intent is signaled. With Health Pages, marketers can reach audiences consuming health content in real-time related to conditions, treatments, and/or OTC categories.
 
 • Health Populations (Contextual Audience): Target audiences who have recently engaged with content for specific health conditions and treatments within the past 3, 15, or 90+ days. Health Populations are built dynamically using the entire browsing profile of the individual, which allows you to capture the user regardless of the page they are on or arriving from.
 
 • Health Populations Plus (Contextual Audience): Combining our Health Populations audiences with endemic health signals coming from Internet Brands owned & operated health sites such as WebMD, to reach a more qualified patient audience.
 
 • Keywords: Real-time keyword targeting based on keywords provided by agency, brand or PulsePoint.
 
 • Keyword Populations: Dynamic audiences that have recently engaged with content containing keywords related to the condition, brand, symptoms, competitors etc. provided by the agency, client, or PulsePoint.

• Flat Bid - Always bid your chosen base bid price (the starting price price)
• Tactic Reach - Maximize unique reach for a tactic by delivering more against users not already exposed
• Line Item Reach - Maximize unique reach for a line item by delivering more against users not already exposed at a tactic level
• Campaign Reach - Maximize unique reach for the total campaign by delivering more against users not already exposed at a tactic level
• Click Through Rate (CTR) - Increase click-through-rates based on specified CTR % goal, also keeping pace a priority
• Clinical Behavior - Optimize ad spend for HCPs most likely to prescribe the target script to increase brand conversion
• Audience Quality - Prioritize ad spend with consumers mostly likely to have a brand-defined condition diagnosis and audience attributes
• CPA - in beta
 
Bid Multipliers can also be applied to: Behavioral Segments, Day of the Week, NPI, Age, Gender, IAB Categories, Keywords, Health Pages, Geo Targets, Browser, Device, Operating Systems, Inventory Source, Domaind and Apps, and Creative Size

records.question: What differentiates your platform/data/media, etc…from your competitors
records.answer:
PulsePoint is the programmatic arm of Internet brands, owner of WebMD/Medscape, and the leader in the health marketing space leveraging proprietary software, data, and analytics to effectively reach your target audience via display, video, native and CTV.
 
 We have an identity graph informed by first-party data through our parent companies WebMD and Medscape, making our offerings future-proofed for the cookie apocalypse. Our contextualizer is mapped to the National Institute of Health’s MESH taxonomy, allowing us to build out 3,500+ condition-based audience segments. We are able to target, measure and report based on 1:1 NPI level against 3.2M NPIs. With our access to claims data, we can target physicians based on certain Dx, Tx, and Rx behaviors. Additionally, we can reach diagnosed patients who are also actively reading about their condition - combining our proprietary contextual technology with raw claims data. 
 
 PulsePoint's programmatic platform integrates seamlessly with our HCP analytics technology, HCP365, which is backed by a database of over 3 million NPIs with active, named opt-in consent. Utilizing proprietary methodologies, HCP365 maps NPIs across various screens and devices, unifying cross-channel insights and providing analysis at the individual HCP level for precise 1:1 attribution. Identified HCPs can then be automatically remarketed to based on predefined business rules.
 
 
 HCP: PulsePoint is the only fully consented and deterministic activation platform with the ability to identify and provide NPI and clinical behavior targeting for authenticated NPI's.

PulsePoint operates both a contextual as well as a deterministic DTC Platform. Similarly, accessing Medscape through the LIFE platform WebMD inventory is also available on LIFE. In addition, WebMD-based audiences (patients visiting WebMD) will be available to Heartbeat.
 Crosswalk: PulsePoint's technology, leveraging signals from WebMD and Medscape and other digitally and clinically relevant sources, is positioned to take advantage of the natural synergy between HCP and DTC audiences who are intrinsically connected throughout the journey toward better overall health outcomes. We enable your agency with the ability to leverage HCP data and insights to inform DTC targeting and visa-versa. This includes solutions customized for clients to reach both the HCPs on the target list and their patients at optimal points in the journey, including at the point of care, between appointments, and in locations where HCPs are seeing a high influx of patients with specific symptoms.

records.question: NPI Match Definition
records.answer:
PulsePoint leverages a first party data foundation at the core of our business. The HCP identity graph uses the power of Medscape's physician member database to authenticate 3.2 million NPI numbers across the United States to inform and validate all HCP targeting from the Life platform. The offline NPI numbers are translated into online IDs within a proprietary identity infrastructure, and campaigns are then able to reach the physicians within their digital footprint. PulsePoint is specifically focused to developing a best-in-class, accurate translation of the NPI number to digital ID, which has generated an NPI graph that has an addressability rate of 92% – 96% on average (i.e. with 10k NPIs, PulsePoint can deliver to 9.5k of those within a 30-day window).
 
 "Addressable Match" in our Life DSP means we have opt-in consent, at least one verified digital ID, and have seen the NPI active online within the past 30 days.

records.question: What does a privacy safe and audience first activation look like in 2025 and beyond?
records.answer:
For Sensitive conditions, we follow NAI guidelines.
 
 https://www.pulsepoint.com/legal/platform-privacy-policy
 
 As far as privacy considerations, we are actively monitoring all new privacy laws and their effective dates, and our legal team reviews the laws and analyzes what needs to be changed in our products, processes, and public-facing disclosures. We have, and will continue to, update our privacy policy to adhere to the requirements of the applicable state laws.
 
 We have implemented the applicable tech specs to recognize GPP (from the IAB), GDPR, CCPA, and other consent strings.  We have increased our geotargeting radius to 2000ft for all states in the US, as most new privacy laws include a definition of “Precise Geolocation” - the exact distance varies from state to state, so we have implemented a 2000ft radius distance to ensure compliance with all states. We are removing certain product availability in Washington State, New York State, and Connecticut to comply with those states’ new prohibitions on geofencing around in-person healthcare facilities.
 
 Our product and tech teams regularly review products with legal counsel to ensure compliance with US privacy laws, including HIPAA, FTC, etc. Our legal team has created processes in conjunction with the business teams to ensure we review any cases where sensitive information or PHI may potentially be collected, and then take the appropriate steps to ensure security and privacy of that information. records.question: DTC audience methodology?
records.answer:
PulsePoint's DTC audience methodology combines medically mapped contextual data, online audience behaviors, clinical data, and signals from Internet Brands' owned and operated health sites, such as WebMD. This multi-source approach enables the identification of consumer audiences based on their medical interests, behaviors, conditions, and engagement with trusted health platforms. By integrating these diverse data points, PulsePoint delivers precise, relevant messaging to target audiences, enhancing the effectiveness of direct-to-consumer (DTC) campaigns.
 
 For DTC:
 - Bespoke Audiences: Clinical signals for DTC are the results of the production of audience models that are optimized in real time toward the prevalence of diagnosis and treatment by age, gender and zip code at delivery. Custom claims-based models based on a database of 220MM+ Patients and 3BB annual pharmacy claims. Audience models created following NAI guidelines for audience/contextual targeting for sensitive conditions.
 -- Life science companies often utilize HCP data to inform DTC audience segmentation. 
 - Health Pages: Capture the consumer & patient’s attention the exact moment intent is signaled. Target audiences consuming relevant health content.
 - Health Populations: Target audiences who have recently engaged with content for specific health conditions and treatments. Populations are built dynamically using the entire browsing profile of the individual, which allows you to capture the user regardless of the page they are on or arriving from.
 - Health Populations+: This takes our foundational Health Populations Audiences and includes their first-party signals through PulsePoint’s proprietary access to endemic website data.
 - Rx Populations: Rx Populations reaches qualified, scalable DTC audiences without sacrificing performance by combining PulsePoint’s contextually created audiences (HealthPop) with RX data to maintain quality and scale, while having a positive impact on AQ during later stage moments of the health journey.
 - OTC Populations: Audience models created following NAI guidelines for audience/contextual targeting for sensitive conditions
 - Keywords: Real-time keyword targeting based on keywords provided by agency, brand or PulsePoint
 - Keyword Populations: Customer audiences that have recently engaged with content containing pre-specified keywords or health specific keywords provided by PulsePoint
 - IBM Watson: Leverage real-world ZIP data where conditions are likely to be impacted by external factors (eg weather)
 
 We also have more generalized targeting capabilities such as retargeting, clickers, converters, IAB, demographic (age, gender, ethnicity), geography etc.

records.question: How are you handling the deprivation of cookies?
records.answer:

records.question: Please list your preferred clean room integrations, if any? Do you support your own clean room product?
records.answer:
PulsePoint integrates with several industry-leading clean room solutions to ensure secure, privacy-compliant data collaboration between brands, agencies, and partners. These clean rooms allow for safe sharing of data without exposing personally identifiable information (PII) or compromising user privacy.
 1. LiveRamp Safe Haven: PulsePoint integrates with LiveRamp’s clean room, which allows advertisers to safely collaborate and analyze data sets for audience insights, measurement, and campaign optimization while ensuring data privacy.
 2. Google Ads Data Hub: For advertisers using Google infrastructure, PulsePoint can work with Google Ads Data Hub to securely match data and analyze performance within a compliant environment.
 3. Snowflake Data Clean Room: PulsePoint has the flexibility to integrate with Snowflake’s clean room capabilities for secure, scalable data collaboration across marketing and advertising data.
 
 Yes, PulsePoint offers its own clean room product, allowing clients to collaborate on data while maintaining stringent privacy controls. PulsePoint’s clean room is specifically designed to support HIPAA compliance and other healthcare data privacy standards. It enables the secure matching of de-identified consumer data (such as claims data or audience segments) with PulsePoint's proprietary datasets for analysis, campaign measurement, and audience insights, without exposing raw data.
 
 This clean room setup is used for privacy-safe targeting and measurement, allowing advertisers to optimize campaigns and measure outcomes, such as prescription lift, in a compliant and secure way.

records.question: What tools do you have to prevent ID spoofing?
records.answer: As well as our Supply Quality Assurance Team and third party verification vendors that prevent ID spoofing, PulsePoint leans on ID graph validation, encrypted ID syncing, and device/IP fingerprinting to prevent fraudulent IDs being attributed to our identity graph. PulsePoint’s Direct Match Identity Graph is powered by first-party opt-in data from trusted sources like Medscape and WebMD. This graph relies on deterministic matching, meaning it directly verifies the identity of healthcare professionals (HCPs) and de-identified consumers through a trusted chain of custody, minimizing the risk of fraudulent identity spoofing. PulsePoint uses encrypted ID synchronization with identity providers such as LiveRamp, ID5, and Unified ID 2.0. This ensures that any identity information shared between PulsePoint and external partners is securely encrypted and cannot be spoofed or tampered with. By using encrypted first-party data, PulsePoint ensures that only validated and authorized users are targeted. To further prevent spoofing, PulsePoint applies device and IP fingerprinting techniques that analyze device characteristics, such as operating systems, browser versions, and IP addresses, to identify potential mismatches or anomalies that might suggest spoofing. This helps detect when a fraudulent user attempts to impersonate a legitimate one.

records.question: How can your DSP remove intermediaries within the supply chain and streamline access to supply across all buying types (Open Exchange, Curated Inventory, PMP's)?
records.answer:
PulsePoint's platform ensures a clean and fair path to supply by focusing on transparency, quality, and efficiency throughout the entire programmatic supply chain. At its core, PulsePoint reduces the number of intermediaries in the bidding process by building direct relationships with premium publishers, particularly those focused on health-related content. This reduces unnecessary layers in the supply chain, minimizing fees and ensuring that advertisers are not paying inflated costs due to multiple parties taking cuts. Lastly, PulsePoint has launched a proprietary solution called Curated Markets that enables partners to leverage unique inventory that best aligns with the brand's KPIs
 
 The platform continuously monitors and evaluates supply sources through its proprietary Supply Quality Avoidance Technology (SQāT). This system is always working behind the scenes to assess the quality and integrity of the inventory, ensuring that any source not meeting strict standards is avoided. This approach helps maintain the highest possible level of inventory quality, while simultaneously safeguarding brands by ensuring their ads only appear in safe and relevant environments.

 The platform continuously monitors and evaluates supply sources through its proprietary Supply Quality Avoidance Technology (SQāT). records.question: Are there tools in platform that help plan to hyper-local campaigns? For inventory across display, OLV, CTV, audio, DOOH?
records.answer:
PulsePoint offers several tools within its platform to help plan and execute hyper-local campaigns across various inventory types, including display, OLV (online video), CTV (connected TV), audio, and DOOH (digital out-of-home). Here are the key features that support hyper-local planning:
 1. Geographic Targeting Tools:
 Zip Code and Radius Targeting: The platform allows advertisers to set specific zip code-level targeting or radius targeting around specific locations (e.g., hospitals, clinics, or pharmacies). This enables a high degree of localization for campaigns across all inventory types.
 DMA (Designated Market Area) Targeting: For broader regional campaigns, DMA targeting helps ensure you're reaching the right audience within specific media markets.
 Geo-Fencing: This tool allows for targeting users within a defined geographic boundary, such as within a few miles of a medical facility or in specific neighborhoods. Geo-fencing can be used across mobile, CTV, and DOOH campaigns to capture highly localized audiences.
 2. Cross-Channel Inventory:
 Display and OLV (Online Video): Hyper-local targeting can be applied to both display and video ads, enabling advertisers to reach consumers within specific geographic regions across web and app environments.
 CTV: Through integrations with CTV publishers and networks, the platform supports hyper-local CTV campaigns, allowing advertisers to serve video ads to specific households or regions based on geographic data.
 Audio: For hyper-local audio campaigns, the platform allows targeting based on location data, reaching consumers through audio streaming platforms and apps.
 DOOH: PulsePoint’s integration with digital out-of-home (DOOH) inventory enables advertisers to serve location-based ads across screens in public spaces, including transit hubs, healthcare facilities, and retail locations.
 3. Forecasting & Media Planning:
 Hyper-Local Forecasting: PulsePoint’s Media Planner tool enables advertisers to forecast campaign reach and performance based on hyper-local geographic settings, giving estimates for impressions, reach, and frequency within specific areas. This helps in planning localized campaigns across different inventory sources, ensuring precise targeting.
 Cross-Channel Budget Allocation: The platform allows advertisers to forecast and allocate budgets across different channels (display, CTV, audio, etc.) while maintaining a hyper-local focus, optimizing spend for maximum impact within the targeted geography.
 4. Custom Segments for Hyper-Local Audiences:
 Health Condition and Behavior-Based Segments: The platform supports custom audience segments based on health conditions or behaviors. When combined with geographic targeting, advertisers can reach users engaging with specific health content within defined local areas, ensuring hyper-local relevance.
 Demographic and Lifestyle Targeting: In addition to health-based data, advertisers can apply filters such as age, gender, and other demographic attributes to further refine their local audience targeting.
 5. Real-Time Location Data for Optimizations:
 Location-Based Reporting: Post-campaign, the platform provides location-based reporting that shows how campaigns performed across different geographic areas. This allows advertisers to optimize future campaigns based on performance in specific regions or neighborhoods.
 Geo-Conversions: For campaigns with foot traffic goals, PulsePoint offers geo-conversion tracking, allowing advertisers to measure how effectively their hyper-local campaign drove users to physical locations, such as clinics or pharmacies.
 By leveraging these tools, PulsePoint enables advertisers to create highly localized and personalized campaigns across a range of inventory types. Whether it's targeting specific zip codes with display ads or serving hyper-local CTV spots to households in a particular neighborhood, the platform ensures precision in both targeting and message delivery.

records.question: How do you use deterministic data and probabilistic data to model your audiences?

records.question: What deterministic data signals do you have against your unique users?
records.answer:
PulsePoint leverages a first-party data foundation at the core of our business. The HCP identity graph uses the power of Medscape's physician member database to authenticate 3.2 million NPI numbers across the United States to inform and validate all HCP targeting from the platform. The offline NPI numbers are translated into online IDs within a proprietary identity infrastructure and through the use of 4x verified onboarders, and campaigns are then able to reach the physicians within their digital footprint. PulsePoint is specifically focused to developing a best-in-class, accurate translation of the NPI number to digital ID, which has generated an NPI graph that has an addressability rate of 90%+ on average (i.e. with 10k NPIs, PulsePoint can deliver to 9.5k of those within a 30-day window). 
 
 Customized consumer audiences are created using claims data signals such as ICD-10 codes, J-Codes, NDC Codes, and CPT codes to develop a seed that is further modeled out based on diagnosis and treatment propensity by age, gender and zip code. The models directly reference our HIPAA compliant database of 220MM+ Patients and 3BB annual pharmacy claims powered by a Foreign data claims data API and are planned and activated according to NAI privacy guidelines. Additional consumer data signals that reference our proprietary HCP database in an anonymized way, such as likely patients of target HCPs, geographical relevance to practice locations of specific HCPs are also leveraged for modeling purposes. Each model is fully customized.

records.question: Specifically - What offline measurement solutions does your platform offer?
records.answer:
PulsePoint offers a range of offline measurement solutions that integrate both clinical and consumer data, enabling comprehensive analysis of campaign effectiveness, particularly for healthcare marketing. Key offline measurement solutions include:
 1. Claims-Based Measurement: PulsePoint partners with Forian to provide claims-based insights. This includes tracking prescription lift and diagnosing behavior changes directly related to campaigns, using data from over 220 million patients, 3 billion annual pharmacy claims, and 2 billion annual medical claims. This allows brands to measure the real-world impact of their digital campaigns on patient behavior and health outcomes.
 2. Test & Control Groups: PulsePoint enables the creation of test and control groups for campaign effectiveness studies. This approach helps determine the incremental impact of advertising by comparing groups exposed to ads versus those who aren't, measuring actual clinical outcomes like prescriptions filled or treatments received.
 3. Komodo Health Integration: PulsePoint integrates with Komodo Health to provide more granular offline measurements, including reach into specific audiences and deeper insights into clinical outcomes, helping to track long-term behavior shifts post-campaign.
 4. In-Geo Performance Tracking: PulsePoint provides geographic-level analysis, particularly when campaigns are tied to specific healthcare facilities or regions. This enables offline measurement by analyzing behaviors like clinic visits or prescription fills in targeted areas.
 5. Linear / CTV Overlap: PulsePoint works with Comscore to understand the overlap and impact of running both offline linear TV buys in conjunction with digital advertising.
 These solutions are designed to provide actionable insights into real-world health outcomes and the tangible effects of marketing efforts on treatment patterns, all while maintaining HIPAA compliance.

 2. Cross-Device Insights: We offer insights into consumer interaction across multiple devices, ensuring targeting remains consistent across mobile, desktop, CTV, and more.
 3. Audience Attributes: Insights into demographics such as age, gender, and zip code, along with behavioral segmentation based on condition-specific content interaction.
 4. Contextual Data: We use our proprietary contextualizer to analyze page-level context, allowing us to create precise and relevant audiences based on the content they engage with, without identifying personal health information.

records.question: Do you have off-the-shelf, condition specific inventory or specialty audience groups that we can apply?
records.answer:
We have a number of different targeting capabilities for both HCP and DTC readily available directly in platform.
 
 For HCP, we have the following:
 - HCP Direct Match for NPI, Specialty, Clinical Behavior and Practice. For NPI, we have deterministic 1:1 NPI targeting, backed up by a database of over 3.2 million HCPs in the US, and with NPI level reporting. For specialty, target and activate your HCP audience based on their primary/secondary specialties and profession. For clinical behavior, target HCPs based on their clinical behavior e.g. prescriptions, diagnoses, procedures etc (Rx, Dx, Px). For practice, target HCPs and HCP decision-makers at their practice and point-of-care facilities.
 
 For DTC, we have the following:
 - Bespoke Audiences: Clinical signals for DTC are the results of the production of audience models that are optimized in real time toward prevalence of diagnosis and treatment by age, gender and zip code at delivery. Custom claims-based models based on a database of 220MM+ Patients and 3BB annual pharmacy claims. Audience models created following NAI guideline for audience/contextual targeting for sensitive conditions.
 - Health Pages: Capture the consumer & patient’s attention the exact moment intent is signaled. Target audiences consuming relevant health content.
 - Health Populations: Target audiences who have recently engaged with content for specific health conditions and treatments. Populations are built dynamically using the entire browsing profile of the individual, which allows you to capture the user regardless of the page they are on or arriving from.
 - Health Populations+: This takes our foundational Health Populations Audiences and includes their first-party signals through PulsePoint’s proprietary access to endemic website data.
 - Rx Populations: Rx Populations reaches qualified, scalable DTC audiences without sacrificing performance by combining PulsePoint’s contextually created audiences (HealthPop) with RX data to maintain quality and scale, while having a positive impact on AQ during later stage moments of the health journey.
 - OTC Populations: Audience models created following NAI guideline for audience/contextual targeting for sensitive conditions
 - Keywords: Real-time keyword targeting based on keywords provided by agency, brand or PulsePoint
 - Keyword Populations: Customer audiences that have recently engaged with content containing pre-specified keywords or health specific keywords provided by PulsePoint
 - IBM Watson: Leverage real-world ZIP data where conditions are likely to be impacted by external factors (eg weather)
 
 We also have more generalized targeting capabilities such as retargeting, clickers, converters, IAB, demographic (age, gender, ethnicity), geography etc.

records.question: Are you working with any partners (ex.Scope3) towards this green initiative?
records.answer:
Our company reuses IT hardware through a structured refurbishment program. This initiative is part of our commitment to sustainability and efficient resource management. 
 When certain IT hardware reaches the end of its initial deployment phase, it undergoes a thorough refurbishment process. This includes diagnosing and repairing any issues, upgrading components as needed, and ensuring that the hardware meets current performance standards. After refurbishment, the equipment is reassigned to other departments or employees who need it, thereby extending its useful life. 
 We have a systematic approach for internal hardware reuse. This involves inventorying and tracking hardware assets, evaluating their condition, and redeploying them where they can still be effectively utilized. We prioritize internal reuse before considering external disposal or recycling options. 
 By refurbishing and reusing IT hardware internally, we reduce electronic waste and minimize the environmental impact of disposing of equipment. 
 We ensure that all refurbished equipment meets our internal quality standards and performs reliably. We also maintain documentation for each refurbishment to ensure transparency and accountability. 
 Employees participate in our internal hardware reuse program by returning old or unused equipment. This engagement helps streamline the refurbishment process and ensures that hardware is effectively redistributed within the company. 
 We continuously review and improve our refurbishment practices to enhance efficiency and effectiveness. This includes staying updated with the latest technologies and best practices in hardware refurbishment and reuse.

 Identity Solutions: PulsePoint integrates with multiple external ID providers, including RampID, UID2, and ID5. This approach allows for seamless identity management and targeting across platforms without dependence on cookies​​​​.
 
 Contextual Targeting: Utilizing the PulsePoint contextualizer, ads are served based on the content of the page rather than user behavior tracking. This ensures relevance and compliance with privacy standards​​.
 
 Cookieless IDs and Single Sign-On: PulsePoint has completed its single sign-on integration with Medscape, enabling the mapping of cookieless IDs to actual identities of healthcare professionals. This allows for accurate targeting and reporting at the physician level even without cookies​​.
 
 Advanced Technologies: The company uses AI and machine learning models to predict user behavior and preferences based on available data points. This strategy does not require tracking individuals across the web, thus maintaining privacy compliance​​.

records.question: How exactly is the PulsePoint tracking tech being used to create lookalike audiences?
records.answer: Based on the data collected as described in section 1, PulsePoint leverages its proprietary device graph to identify devices that share similar characteristics to the devices observed on the website. These devices are aggregated anonymously to develop an audience for lookalike models.

records.question: What and how will this (pixel) information be shared with PulsePoint?
records.answer:
PulsePoint collects data through cookies, which are small data files stored by the site visitor’s web browser on the site visitor’s computer. When a user visits the website with a retargeting pixel installed, the pixel triggers and collects data based on the user’s interactions, device information, and other relevant details.
The data collected is transmitted to our server via HTTP and HTTPs requests. Once the data reaches the server it is processed and stored compliantly. Data privacy and security are critical to PulsePoint. Please reference the links above for more details.

records.question: What specific user information will be collected via the Pulsepoint-provided tracking tech from our websites?
records.answer:
The information we collect is either non-PII, which is data that does not identify the individual in any way but is associated with the user’s browsing behavior, or pseudonymous personal data.
This includes:
·       Websites the user has visited and related information, such as pages visited or the time of day the user visited the website;
·       PulsePoint Ads served, viewed, or clicked on
·       The time of day of the user’s visit
·       Apps visited
·       The start and stop time of a use session
·       The user’s time zone and network connection type
·       Mobile device information, such as the type and model, software version, manufacturer, operating system (e.g., iOS or Android), carrier name, mobile browser (e.g., Chrome or Safari), applications used and the version of such applications, and identifiers assigned to the user’s device, such as its iOS Identifier for Advertising (IDFA), Android Advertising ID (AAID), or unique device identifier (a number uniquely given to your device by your device manufacturer), sometimes referred to as a mobile carrier ID
·       The user’s Internet protocol (IP) address;
·       Location information, such as the user’s zip code or approximate geographic area provided by the user’s ISP or by location services and GPS features of a website or mobile device. GPS location may be shared with us if a site visitor has opted to provide that information to a publisher or other content provider who is responsible for obtaining the site visitor’s prior permission to share that data with us. We may also infer geolocation of your device based on data collected through, for example, a WiFi identifier
A user has several choices when it comes to opting out of the collection of information about web browsing activities through cookies. Consumers are also able to opt out of data collection at any time.

records.question:
Provide an overview of your healthcare compliance program as it relates to the Federal Food, Drug, & Cosmetic Act, the Anti-kickback Statute, and HIPAA and applicable state privacy laws, including:
          Remediation (e.g., Describe types of corrective actions your organization takes for non-compliance of your personnel? How do you communicate non-compliance to your clients?)
records.answer:
All employees are required to take training 4 times annually to educate about ethical business practices.
Our legal team regularly provides presentations on new laws and changes to the way we must operate in order to comply. Our internal legal counsel is also always available to the team to answer questions.
 
Our legal teams use trackers and meet regularly (at least once per month, sometimes more often) to review existing and new laws and to review our policies. PulsePoint’s legal counsel is deeply entrenched in the business and works with the Product, Data and Sales teams daily to aid in monitoring compliance with applicable laws. The compliance group also meets weekly to discuss any issues or review projects to maintain compliance.
 
If instances of non-compliance were to occur, we undertake a comprehensive remediation process that includes 1) internal review and investigation; 2) training and education; 3) disciplinary actions, if necessary; 4) process improvements. 
To maintain transparency and trust with our clients, we communicate instances of non-compliance in a timely and clear manner. This communication would include a detailed explanation of the issue, the steps we are taking to address it, and the measures we plan to implement to prevent recurrence.

records.question: If an individual has opted out, what information is still collected on them, if any?

records.question: Please describe how you are ensuring privacy compliance with current privacy legislations (GDPR, CCPA, etc.)
records.answer:
We are actively monitoring all new privacy laws and their effective dates, and our legal team reviews the laws and analyzes what needs to be changed in our products, processes and public-facing disclosures. 
 We have, and will continue to, update our privacy policy in order to adhere to requirements of the applicable state laws.
 We have implemented the applicable tech specs to recognize GPP (from the IAB), GDPR, CCPA, and other consent strings.
 PulsePoint is a signatory to the MSPA (from the IAB), which helps aid in ensuring contractual obligations are in place as required by the new state privacy laws.
 PulsePoint has implemented and uses OneTrust as its Consent Management Platform, which includes cookie management and opt-outs for its owned and operated sites. 
 We have increased our geotargeting radius to 2000ft for all states in the US, as most new privacy laws include a definition of “Precise Geolocation” - the exact distance varies from state to state, so we have implemented a 2000ft radius distance to ensure compliance with all states. 
 We have removed certain product availability to comply with states’ new prohibitions on geofencing around in-person health care facilities.
 Our product and tech teams regularly review products with legal counsel to ensure compliance with US privacy laws, including HIPAA, FTC, etc. 
 Our legal team has created processes in conjunction with the business teams to ensure we review any cases where sensitive information or PHI may potentially be collected, and then take the appropriate steps to ensure security and privacy of that information. 
 We honor all validated opt outs received by consumers, both via CMPs and AdChoices as well as emails to our privacy@pulsepoint.com inbox.

records.question: How do you build your audience segments?

records.question: What is PulsePoint's Value Proposition?
records.answer:
HCP: PulsePoint is the only fully consented and deterministic activation platform with the ability to identify and provide NPI and clinical behavior targeting for 1st party authenticated NPI's. PulsePoint is the only DSP integrated with Medscape for data and inventory and is the exclusive DSP for Medscape buying, offering the largest endemic programmatic scale and reach in the industry.
 
 DTC: PulsePoint is the only first-party validated platform providing a journey-based product suite of targeting and attribution technology. PulsePoint operates both a contextual as well as a deterministic DTC Platform. WebMD-based inventory and audiences (patients visiting WebMD) will be available to Klick.
 
 Crosswalk: PulsePoint's technology, leveraging signals from WebMD and Medscape and other digitally and clinically relevant sources, is positioned to take advantage of the natural synergy between HCP and DTC audiences who are intrinsically connected throughout the journey toward better overall health outcomes. We enable your agency with the ability to leverage HCP data and insights to inform DTC targeting and visa-versa. This includes solutions customized for clients to reach both the HCPs on the target list and their patients at optimal points in the journey, including at the point of care, between appointments, and in locations where HCPs are seeing a high influx of patients with specific symptoms.

records.question: O&O Offering
records.answer:
We have an identity graph informed by first-party data through our parent companies WebMD and Medscape, making our offerings future-proofed.
 
 Our contextualizer is mapped to the National Institute of Health’s MESH taxonomy, allowing us to build out 3,500+ condition-based audience segments. We are able to target, measure and report based on 1:1 NPI level against 3.2M opt-in, 1st party authenticated NPIs. 
 
 With our access to claims data, we can target physicians based on certain Dx, Tx, and Rx behaviors alongsite search and site behaviors. Additionally, we can reach diagnosed & treating patients who are also actively engaged with their condition - combining our proprietary contextual technology with raw claims data.

records.question: AI - Machine Learning  - Programs/systems that can improve their performance on a specific task over time without being explicitly programmed to do so
records.answer:
• Predictive Analytics and Behavior Modeling: PulsePoint's platform uses machine learning to analyze vast datasets to predict healthcare professionals' and patients' future media behaviors, interests, and clinical needs.
• Contextual Targeting: PulsePoint's contextualizer understands and interprets the content of web pages at a granular level. This capability enables the platform to place ads in the most relevant online environments automatically, improving engagement without manual intervention for content matching.
• Audience Segmentation: By leveraging machine learning, PulsePoint can dynamically segment audiences based on evolving patterns in data, such as changes in media behavior, clinical health data and content engagement. 
• Cross-Device Identification and Targeting: Machine learning allows PulsePoint to accurately identify and target individuals across devices and platforms, ensuring consistent messaging and improved user experiences.
• Automated Campaign Pacing: PulsePoint incorporates automated pacing technologies to ensure that campaign spending is optimized over the duration of the campaign. PulsePoint automatically adjusts the rate of ad delivery based on predefined budget limits, campaign dates and user pacing preferences.

records.question: AI - Basic Task Automation - Programs/systems that perform predefined tasks or processes without human intervention, based on explicit instructions and rules.
records.answer:
• Data Management: PulsePoint automates the creation and management of NPI lists in many ways. Our smart list capability allows a user to select different criteria to form a list, and PulsePoint will continuously keep that list up to date. Pulsepoint also manages internal data automatically to create different segments and audiences based on different 1st and 3rd party data sets. 
• Integration and Data Synchronization: PulsePoint automates the process of integrating with external data sources and platforms. PulsePoint also offers an NPI list API which allows clients to sync their most up to date NPI list with PulsePoint seamlessly, limiting any human interaction and adjusting targeting lists on the fly as directed by the Client’s own systems. 
• Compliance and Brand Safety: PulsePoint uses automated tools and partners to ensure ads are placed in brand-safe environments and in compliance with regulatory standards. 
• Reporting and Analytics: The platform automates the generation of detailed reports and analytics, providing insights into campaign performance, audience behavior, and market trends. This automation saves time and resources, allowing marketers to quickly adjust strategies based on actionable data.

records.question: Please list all demographics and specific audience groups your properties have the largest reach against:
records.answer:
We have a number of different targeting capabilities for both HCP and DTC. 
 
For HCP, we have the following:
- HCP Direct Match for NPI, Specialty, Clinical Behavior and Practice. For NPI, we have deterministic 1:1 NPI targeting, backed up by a database of over 3.2 million HCPs in the US, and with NPI level reporting. For specialty, target and activate your HCP audience based on their primary/secondary specialties and profession. For clinical behavior, target HCPs based on their clinical behavior e.g. prescriptions, diagnoses, procedures etc (Rx, Dx, Px). For practice, target HCPs and HCP decision-makers at their practice and point-of-care facilities.
 
For DTC, we have the following:
- Bespoke Audiences: Clinical signals for DTC are the results of the production of audience models that are optimized in real time toward prevalence of diagnosis and treatment by age, gender and zip code at delivery. Custom claims-based models based on a database of 220MM+ Patients and 3BB annual pharmacy claims. Audience models created following NAI guideline for audience/contextual targeting for sensitive conditions.
- Health Pages: Capture the consumer & patient’s attention the exact moment intent is signaled. Target audiences consuming relevant health content.
- Health Populations: Target audiences who have recently engaged with content for specific health conditions and treatments. Populations are built dynamically using the entire browsing profile of the individual, which allows you to capture the user regardless of the page they are on or arriving from.
- Health Populations+: This takes our foundational Health Populations Audiences and includes their first-party signals through PulsePoint’s proprietary access to endemic website data.
- Rx Populations: Rx Populations reaches qualified, scalable DTC audiences without sacrificing performance by combining PulsePoint’s contextually created audiences (HealthPop) with RX data to maintain quality and scale, while having a positive impact on AQ during later stage moments of the health journey.
- OTC Populations: Audience models created following NAI guideline for audience/contextual targeting for sensitive conditions
- Keywords: Real-time keyword targeting based on keywords provided by agency, brand or PulsePoint
- Keyword Populations: Customer audiences that have recently engaged with content containing pre-specified keywords or health specific keywords provided by PulsePoint
- IBM Watson: Leverage real-world ZIP data where conditions are likely to be impacted by external factors (eg weather)
 
We also have more generalized targeting capabilities such as retargeting, clickers, converters, IAB, demographic (age, gender, ethnicity), geography etc.

records.question: What is the methodology behind your segment creation? (Ex. Use a seed audience that is then modeled out for distribution)
records.answer:
PulsePoint leverages a first party data foundation at the core of our business. The HCP identity graph uses the power of Medscape's physician member database to authenticate 3.2 million NPI numbers across the United States to inform and validate all HCP targeting from platform. The offline NPI numbers are translated into online IDs within a proprietary identity infrastructure and through the use of 4x verified onboarders, and campaigns are then able to reach the physicians within their digital footprint. PulsePoint is specifically focused to developing a best-in-class, accurate translation of the NPI number to digital ID, which has generated an NPI graph that has an addressability rate of 90%+ on average (i.e. with 10k NPIs, PulsePoint can deliver to 9.5k of those within a 30-day window). 
 
 Customized consumer audiences are created using claims data signals such as ICD-10 codes, J-Codes, NDC Codes, and CPT codes to develop a seed that is further modeled out based on diagnosis and treatment propensity by age, gender and zip code. The models directly reference our HIPPA compliant database of 220MM+ Patients and 3BB annual pharmacy claims powered by a Forian data claims data API and are planned and activated according to NAI privacy guidelines. Additional consumer data signals that reference our proprietary HCP database in an anonymized way, such as likely patients of target HCPs, geographical relevance to practice locations of specific HCPs are also leveraged for modeling purposes. Each model is fully customized.

records.question: What's your data collection methodology?
records.answer: PulsePoint delivers deterministic, people-based HCP data targeting by validating identities and attribution of nearly every digitally connected healthcare professional by NPI number. We receive opt-in consent directly from the individual not through multiple intermediaries. When you target NPIs using PulsePoint’s technology and data methodology you're targeting from the source of opt-in consent. records.question: What data is fueling your identify graph?
records.answer:
PulsePoint leverages a first party data foundation at the core of our business. The HCP identity graph uses the power of Medscape's physician member database to authenticate 3.2 million NPI numbers across the United States to inform and validate all HCP targeting from platform. The offline NPI numbers are translated into online IDs within a proprietary identity infrastructure and through the use of 4x verified onboarders, and campaigns are then able to reach the physicians within their digital footprint. PulsePoint is specifically focused to developing a best-in-class, accurate translation of the NPI number to digital ID, which has generated an NPI graph that has an addressability rate of 90%+ on average (i.e. with 10k NPIs, PulsePoint can deliver to 9.5k of those within a 30-day window). 
 
 Customized consumer audiences are created using claims data signals such as ICD-10 codes, J-Codes, NDC Codes, and CPT codes to develop a seed that is further modeled out based on diagnosis and treatment propensity by age, gender and zip code. The models directly reference our HIPAA compliant database of 220MM+ Patients and 3BB annual pharmacy claims powered by a Foreign data claims data API and are planned and activated according to NAI privacy guidelines. Additional consumer data signals that reference our proprietary HCP database in an anonymized way, such as likely patients of target HCPs, geographical relevance to practice locations of specific HCPs are also leveraged for modeling purposes. Each model is fully customized.

records.question: Can you detail your reporting capabilities or share an example?
records.answer:
PulsePoint’s reporting capabilities provide a comprehensive and real-time view of campaign performance, enabling advertisers to track and optimize their efforts across various channels, devices, and audience segments. The reporting is designed to be highly granular, offering insights into impressions, engagement, conversions, audience behaviors, and health-related outcomes.
 
Key Reporting Features:
1) Real-Time Reporting Dashboards:
PulsePoint offers real-time dashboards that provide up-to-the-minute insights into campaign metrics such as impressions, clicks, click-through rates (CTR), and conversions. These dashboards allow for immediate adjustments to campaigns based on live data.
2) Audience Segmentation & Performance:
The reporting platform offers detailed insights into how specific audience segments perform, allowing advertisers to analyze engagement rates by segments such as de-identified consumers, healthcare professionals (HCPs), and condition-based targeting. Advertisers can also view performance by demographics (e.g., age, gender) and behaviors (e.g., content interactions).
3) Site-Level and Placement Insights:
Advertisers can see exactly where their ads were served, including details at the site, app, or page level. This helps understand the quality and context of inventory sources. In addition, placement data such as whether ads were above or below the fold can be tracked.
4) Cross-Channel and Device Reporting:
PulsePoint provides a cross-channel view, enabling advertisers to see how their campaigns are performing across display, video, connected TV (CTV), digital out-of-home (DOOH), and mobile. Device-level data (e.g., mobile, desktop, tablet, CTV) also ensures that campaigns can be optimized based on device performance.
5) Viewability and Brand Safety Metrics:
Integrated with verification partners such as DoubleVerify, the platform tracks viewability rates, fraud detection, and brand safety compliance. These metrics help ensure that campaigns are served in trusted environments and reach the intended audience.
6) Geographic and Demographic Reporting:
Advertisers can view campaign performance at a geographic level, from national to zip code, allowing for precise regional insights. Similarly, demographic data provides insights into how different groups within the target audience are interacting with the campaign.
7) Post-Engagement and Health Outcomes:
For healthcare campaigns, PulsePoint offers advanced insights into post-engagement behaviors, such as prescription lift or visits to health-related sites. Integrated data partnerships enable advertisers to measure actual health outcomes based on ad exposure.
 
Sample Metrics in Reports:
Impressions
Clicks and CTR
Viewability Rate
Conversions (e.g., form fills, downloads)
Audience Breakdown (by age, gender, conditions)
Geographic Reach (country, state, zip code)
Device Performance (mobile, desktop, CTV, etc.)
Ad Placement Data (above/below fold)
Frequency & Recency
 
PulsePoint’s reporting can also be customized based on specific KPIs and goals. Additionally, advertisers can use the API to export reports into external systems or BI tools for further analysis, ensuring seamless integration with your internal data workflows.

records.question:
Please provide an executive summary of the services your company provides. Please highlight some of the
innovative and successful approaches you have used in the past that differentiate you from other partners in
this space. Which companies do you consider to be your main competitors and what do you consider as your
competitive advantages relative to them?
records.answer:
PulsePoint is a leading healthcare programmatic technology company, specializing in the fusion of health data, AI, and programmatic media to deliver precision-targeted advertising campaigns. Our platform enables healthcare brands and agencies to engage both Healthcare Professionals (HCPs) and de-identified consumers based on real-time behavior, intent, and context across digital channels. PulsePoint’s technology processes over 300 billion daily signals from digital touchpoints to drive high-quality, compliant marketing outcomes.
 
Our core services include:
1) Programmatic Advertising: End-to-end programmatic solutions that allow for precise audience targeting across display, video, CTV, mobile, and other digital media, optimized in real-time for performance.
2) Data Solutions: We leverage proprietary first-party health data from platforms like WebMD and Medscape, as well as external data integrations, to offer unmatched audience insights and segmentation capabilities.
3) Audience Targeting & Activation: Using de-identified health data, we create customized audience segments based on health conditions, demographics, and behavior to optimize campaign delivery.
4) Real-Time Analytics & Reporting: We provide deep, actionable insights through comprehensive reporting on campaign performance, user engagement, and health outcomes, enabling brands to optimize their media investments.
 
Innovative Approaches that Differentiate PulsePoint:
1) Proprietary Data Integration: PulsePoint’s access to first-party data from WebMD and Medscape allows us to deliver insights and targeting that is unparalleled in the healthcare space. This data foundation enables precise targeting of de-identified consumer and HCP audiences based on real-time behavior and intent signals across thousands of health-related conditions and interests.
2) AI-Powered Contextual Targeting: We leverage our patented contextualizer tool, which interprets health-related content across millions of web pages in real time. By using natural language processing (NLP) and AI, we ensure that ads are served in highly relevant contexts, avoiding keyword misalignment and ensuring brand safety. This allows healthcare marketers to deliver personalized, relevant messages aligned with specific health conditions.
3) Cookieless Solutions: As the industry moves away from third-party cookies, PulsePoint is at the forefront of developing cookieless targeting solutions through identity-based and contextual targeting. Our proprietary Genome technology and ID Consortium partnerships (e.g., LiveRamp, Unified ID 2.0) ensure effective audience reach in a privacy-compliant, future-proof way.
4) Compliance and Privacy: PulsePoint is fully HIPAA-compliant and a member of the NAI (Network Advertising Initiative). We prioritize privacy and security by working with de-identified data and ensuring all marketing activities comply with the highest industry standards.
 
Main Competitors: Healthcare-focused DSPs and data providers, major industry DSPs
 
Competitive Advantages:
1) First-Party Data Access: Unlike many competitors, PulsePoint benefits from exclusive first-party health data from WebMD and Medscape, giving us a significant edge in terms of audience quality and targeting accuracy. This integration ensures that we can build precise, de-identified consumer and HCP segments across the healthcare journey.
2) Real-Time Optimization: PulsePoint’s platform provides real-time analytics and the ability to optimize campaigns dynamically. Our Real-Time Intelligence Loop continuously refines audience targeting and bidding strategies, leading to higher engagement and ROI compared to traditional methods.
3) Focus on Healthcare Compliance: While many of our competitors offer general programmatic services, PulsePoint is laser-focused on healthcare marketing, ensuring all data and targeting practices are HIPAA-compliant. Our expertise in navigating the complexities of healthcare advertising regulations sets us apart in terms of trust and reliability.
4) Endemic Publisher Network: Our endemic health network allows us to serve ads in trusted environments, providing higher relevance and credibility, particularly for healthcare audiences. This positions us ahead of non-endemic competitors like The Trade Desk, which cannot offer the same level of content relevance.
 
PulsePoint offers unmatched targeting precision, first-party health data integration, and cutting-edge compliance, making it a premier choice for healthcare marketers seeking effective, privacy-compliant programmatic solutions.

records.question: How does your AI model handle data privacy, security, and bias mitigation?
records.answer:
"PulsePoint is committed to operating in a privacy-by-design framework. Our AI solutions exclusively leverage de-identified claims data, never using personal health information (PHI) directly. We align our practices to HIPAA guidelines, are long-standing members of the NAI, and follow rigorous standards in accordance with state-specific privacy laws so that all audience targeting and AI processing respects both consumer privacy and regulatory obligations. Our data flows and pixeling protocols are vetted to avoid placement on sensitive or inappropriate content pages, and any use of inferred targeting (e.g., condition interest) is built to avoid crossing into non-compliant data practices.
For bias mitigation, PulsePoint's AI is continuously audited for fairness in decision-making—especially in clinical or demographic targeting scenarios. Because the healthcare space has unique sensitivities, our AI models are trained on a diversified data foundation that avoids reinforcing stereotypes or excluding high-value audiences due to systemic data gaps. Additionally, we incorporate safeguards into model deployment to ensure transparency in how audiences are built and optimized, enabling marketers to retain control and visibility at all times."

records.question: How is your data sourced?
records.answer:
HCP Data Sources – PulsePoint’s HCP identity graph is built on Medscape’s verified physician membership, encompassing over 4M NPIs with deterministic validation. Each NPI is enriched with affiliation, specialty, subspecialty, and profession attributes, then cross-mapped to personal, household, and work devices for omnichannel addressability. All HCP data is first-party or partner-consented and cookieless-ready via ID consortium participation.
 
Consumer Data Sources – PulsePoint’s consumer dataset is composed of de-identified claims, in alignment with legal and regulatory compliance health interest and intent signals sourced from a blend of proprietary and partner data. This includes contextual and behavioral signals from endemic and non-endemic health publishers and engagement across digital channels. Condition and interest targeting is inferred through content consumption patterns, ensuring no direct use of PHI. Partner integrations add demographic, geographic, and lifestyle enrichment, while While Forian data helps power our own proprietary clinical modelling offerings. Consumer identity resolution uses cookieless IDs, cross-device mapping, and curated data partnerships to maintain reach and measurement accuracy across display, video, CTV, and emerging channels under all applicable privacy regulations.

records.question: Do you use a probabilistic, deterministic, or a hybrid method?
records.answer:
For HCP audiences, deterministic methods are used, such as Direct Match to verified NPI data, ensuring accuracy in identifying, reaching and reporting on specific healthcare professionals 1-1 and in alignment with legal and regulatory compliance.
 
For DTC audiences, we combine deterministic matches (for example, opt-in subscriber or registered user data from trusted partners) with probabilistic modeling to expand reach. Probabilistic methods use aggregated signals like device type, content engagement, and location patterns to infer likely audience membership while maintaining compliance.

records.question: If applicable, how is your contextual data sourced?
records.answer: PulsePoint's contextual data is sourced through our proprietary contextualizer, which is mapped to the National Institute of Health's MeSH taxonomy. This technology allows PulsePoint to read and scan pages for over 3,500 condition relevances, offering solutions such as real-time contextual health pages and segmented health populations based on condition-type content and consumption time frames.

records.question: How do you approach rare disease or low-volume conditions differently than high-volume categories?

records.question: What steps do you take to ensure ongoing compliance with GDPR, CCPA, and other regulations?
records.answer:
– We actively monitor all new privacy laws and their effective dates, with our legal team reviewing the laws and analyzing necessary changes to our products, processes, and public-facing disclosures. 
– Our privacy policy is regularly updated to adhere to the requirements of applicable state laws. 
– We have implemented tech specifications to recognize GPP (from the IAB), GDPR, CCPA, and other consent strings. 
– PulsePoint is a signatory to the MSPA (from the IAB), ensuring contractual obligations are in place as required by new state privacy laws. 
– We use OneTrust as our Consent Management Platform, which includes cookie management and opt-outs for our owned and operated sites. 
– Our geotargeting radius has been increased to 2006ft to comply with definitions of "Precise Geolocation" in various state laws. 
– We have removed certain product availability to comply with prohibitions on geofencing around in-person health care facilities. 
– Our product and tech teams regularly review products with legal counsel to ensure compliance with US privacy laws, including HIPAA and FTC regulations. 
– We have processes to review cases where sensitive information or PHI may be collected, ensuring security and privacy. 
– We honor all validated opt-outs received by consumers through CMPs, AdChoices, and emails to our privacy inbox. 
– We have a cross-functional group that includes Legal, Information Security, and Technology team members that meets regularly to review projects and update policies. 
– Our legal teams use trackers and meet regularly to review existing and new laws and to review our policies. 
– All employees are required to take training four times annually to educate about ethical business practices, with regular presentations on new laws and compliance changes.

records.question: Do you use tokenization or third-party identity resolution?
records.answer:
Yes. PulsePoint uses both tokenization and third party identity resolution to securely match and activate audiences.
 
Tokenization replaces any personally identifiable information with pseudonymous  IDs.
 
For identity resolution, we work with approved third party partners to match first party and third party data across devices and channels. This process allows us to connect deterministic identifiers like NPIs or hashed HCP emails with probabilistic signals, enabling a unified, privacy-preserving  view of the audience.
 
Both processes are in alignment with legal and regulatory compliance.

records.question: What are your state level privacy laws?
records.answer: Our legal teams use trackers and meet regularly (at least once per month, sometimes more often) to review existing and new laws and to review our policies. PulsePoint’s legal counsel is deeply entrenched in the business and works with the Product, Data and Sales teams daily to aid in monitoring compliance with applicable laws. The compliance group also meets weekly to discuss any issues or review projects to maintain compliance.

records.question: Is your data HIPAA-compliant and de-identified to regulatory standards?
records.answer: PulsePoint's data is used in alignment with legal and regulatory compliance.   Modeled data based on de-identified claims data is used so that sensitive information is dropped from claims files, and personal identifiers are replaced by tokens, making it impossible to re-identify individuals later on. Additionally, PulsePoint works with an expert third-party partner to certify and determine that our use cases maintain the separation of data and deidentification standards as defined by HIPAA.

HCP:
 
Target List
Real-time 1-1 targeting of HCPs by NPI number; used for client NPI lists or custom lists developed by PulsePoint DirectMatch™
 
Specialty
Real-time targeting of HCPs by Specialty or Practitioner Type

Audience segment of the likely practice staff of any given HCP list; Enables reach to non-NPI based professionals who work in the same practice as the target HCP
 
NPI Smart Lists™
Automates NPI list creation through real-time signals for digital engagement with a brand and/or claims data, layered with unique NPI attributes. SmartLists allow for customization across multiple factors outlined below:
 
Engagement-based (Pixel) Smart Lists
Unlimited real-time targetable NPI lists based on HCPs who have engaged with brand owned (site) and paid (search) content; Fully customizable
 
Clinical Behavior
Dynamic NPI lists based on claims criteria (Dx, Rx, Tx) and business rules; Ability to mix and match all attributes
 
Top Prescribers / Droppers
Real-time targetable NPI lists based on the top prescribers or droppers of a specified drug/treatment
 
Specialty / Profession
Real-time targetable NPI lists based on HCPs specialty or professions
 
 Endemic Research
Generate a target list by identifying HCPs who have recently engaged with condition-specific content from trusted endemic sources
 
 
DTC:
 
Health Populations
Reach audiences visiting related, condition-based content (Health Pages) across the internet for 3000+ health conditions, and segment by condition type and timeframe consumption habits (3, 15, and 90+ days).
 
Health Populations Plus
Audiences visiting related, condition-based content (Health Pages) across the internet for 3000+ health conditions, (PLUS) visited an owned and operated IB endemic health website, and segment by condition type and timeframe consumption habits (3, 15, and 90+ days).
 
Bespoke Audiences (Clinical Models)
Custom claims-based models based on a database of 220MM+ consumers and 3BB annual pharmacy claims using clinical definitions and/or NPI lists as an input into the model
 
Health Pages (contextual)
Reach audiences on specific web pages, across 3000+ health conditions within NLM's MeSH Taxonomy, in the moment of content consumption.
 
Lookalike Audiences
Data models created to target consumers with the greatest likelihood of digital brand engagement and conversion

records.question: Does your DSP support healthcare professional targeting, including National Provider Identifier (NPI) targeting?

Our sophisticated data technology combines multiple points of online behavior, interest, and first-party permissioned data to validate the identity of HCPs by NPI number. Data sets are refreshed every 24 hours to account for any physicians choosing to opt out of targeting.Yes,

records.question: What level of detail is available (e.g., specialty, prescribing behavior, practice location)?
